claims.claim: Wen-Hua Zhang is dean of Yunnan University’s school of materials and energy in Kunming, China.
claims.episode_span: Wen-Hua Zhang, dean of Yunnan University’s school of materials and energy in Kunming, China, led the work on perovskite solar cells tuned specifically to the blue-green wavelengths between 400 and 600 nanometers that reach five to ten meters below the surface.
claims.source_title: Underwater Solar Cells Capture Energy 10 Meters Below the Surface
claims.supporting_quote: “With submerged solar cells, submarines or autonomous underwater vehicles could achieve far greater range and mission endurance than they do today,” says Wen-Hua Zhang , dean of Yunnan University’s school of materials and energy in Kunming, China.

claims.claim: The perovskite cells achieved 34.71 percent efficiency at ten meters underwater compared with 17.08 percent under terrestrial sunlight.
claims.episode_span: Under standard terrestrial illumination the same cells achieved 17.08 percent conversion efficiency; when illuminated with the underwater spectrum at ten meters depth they reached 34.71 percent efficiency, exceeding typical land-based panel averages of 20 to 25 percent.
claims.source_title: Underwater Solar Cells Capture Energy 10 Meters Below the Surface
claims.supporting_quote: The scientists found that while their photovoltaic cells attained a light-to-electricity conversion efficiency of 17.08 percent under the conditions usually found on land, they achieved 34.71 percent efficiency when given the spectrum of light one would expect submerged 10 meters underwater.

claims.claim: At ten meters depth the encapsulated cells produced 324 milliwatt-hours over two hours.
claims.episode_span: At two meters depth, 115 square centimeters of encapsulated cells produced 1,416 milliwatt-hours over two hours; at ten meters the same area still delivered 324 milliwatt-hours over the same interval.
claims.source_title: Underwater Solar Cells Capture Energy 10 Meters Below the Surface
claims.supporting_quote: At a depth of 2 meters, 115 square centimeters of these encapsulated cells could generate a modest 1,416 milliwatt-hours over two hours—roughly half the capacity of a rechargeable AA battery; at a depth of 10 meters, these cells could still generate 324 mWh of energy over two hours.

claims.claim: Laboratory tests at 25 °C suggest the cells could retain 80 percent of original output after roughly 5.5 years of continuous underwater use.
claims.episode_span: Laboratory aging tests at 25 degrees Celsius, the annual average water temperature near the test site, indicated the cells could operate continuously for roughly 5.5 years before dropping to 80 percent of initial output.
claims.source_title: Underwater Solar Cells Capture Energy 10 Meters Below the Surface
claims.supporting_quote: Given the minimal level of degradation the researchers saw at standard operating temperatures of 25 °C—the annual average water temperature near Weizhou Island—they estimated the cells were capable of continuously operating for roughly 5.5 years before degrading to 80 percent of their original efficiency.

claims.claim: The findings were published on 11 September in the journal Joule.
claims.episode_span: The team published the results on 11 September in the journal Joule and called for standardized testing protocols so different laboratories can compare performance directly.
claims.source_title: Underwater Solar Cells Capture Energy 10 Meters Below the Surface
claims.supporting_quote: The scientists detailed their findings on 11 September in the journal Joule .
